children: Crude oil futures fell Monday for the fourth straight session after President Trump reportedly decided against bombing Yemen for now and indicated he was open to diplomacy with Iran.
Trump has decided against bombing Iran-backed Houthi militants despite pleas from Saudi Arabia, according to
, and the president told Fox News he would consider meeting with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, who is expected to come to New York this week for the United Nations General Assembly.
However, fighting in the Middle East continued as the Houthis said ​they had attacked the Saudi capital Riyadh as well as an Aramco facility in Yanbu on the Red Sea.

"Profit-taking after recent gains, together with hopes for constructive discussions at this week's U.N. General Assembly and the upcoming Trump-Xi meeting, helped improve market sentiment," ING analysts said in a note, although disruptions to Saudi supply due to attacks on its East-West pipeline continue to fuel concerns.

With the pipeline impaired, Saudi Arabia is increasingly relying on its Persian Gulf export terminals to keep crude moving through the Strait of Hormuz; according to Kpler, Saudi oil loadings from the Persian Gulf have jumped by nearly 2M bbl/day to 2.46M bbl/day so far this month, and ship-to-ship volumes from the Gulf of Oman have increased by 1.1M bbl/day since August to 2.5M bbl/day.

Meanwhile, U.S. diesel prices hit a new record of $6.51/gal, AAA reported, as prolonged disruptions to Middle East energy flows and Russian refineries continue to tighten global supplies ahead of winter.
